#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
#
# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    # For every file in our overlay tree, remove any same-basename file
    # in the target that has a DIFFERENT extension. Android's resource
    # merger treats `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher.webp` in the same
    # density bucket as duplicates of the `ic_launcher` resource and
    # fails the build. The dx-generated tree ships defaults as .webp,
    # but a prior overlay run that placed .png files will leave them in
    # the target on subsequent builds (dx doesn't clean). This sweep
    # makes the overlay self-healing — pruning stale variants before
    # copying our canonical extension.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' overlay_file; do
        rel="${overlay_file#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}"
        rel_dir=$(dirname "$rel")
        full_base=$(basename "$rel")
        base="${full_base%.*}"
        ext="${full_base##*.}"
        target_dir="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/$rel_dir"
        if [[ -d "$target_dir" ]]; then
            for stale in "$target_dir/$base".*; do
                if [[ -f "$stale" && "${stale##*.}" != "$ext" ]]; then
                    rm "$stale"
                fi
            done
        fi
    done < <(find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -type f -print0)
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay (pruned stale duplicate-extension variants)"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"

# 3. Variant transforms (River = release / production; River Debug = debug).
#    Controlled by RIVER_VARIANT env var (default: release). The debug
#    variant ships side-by-side with release via a `.debug` applicationId
#    suffix, a distinct launcher label ("River Debug"), and an orange
#    adaptive-icon background so the two installs are visually
#    distinguishable on the home screen.
#
#    All edits write OVER the release-default files copied above, so the
#    release path is left untouched and any future overlay file change
#    lands first; the debug overrides come on top.
RIVER_VARIANT=${RIVER_VARIANT:-release}
echo "  Variant:         $RIVER_VARIANT"

case "$RIVER_VARIANT" in
    release)
        : # nothing to do — overlay defaults already are release
        ;;
    debug)
        # Launcher / activity label.
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml" <<'STRINGS_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh for RIVER_VARIANT=debug.
  Do not edit by hand — edit the heredoc in that script instead.
-->
<resources>
    <string name="app_name">River Debug</string>
</resources>
STRINGS_EOF

        # Adaptive-icon background color (Android 8+). For release we
        # keep the user-supplied solid-white WebP. For debug we swap the
        # adaptive-icon XML to point at a color resource and define that
        # color via colors.xml — same dolphin foreground, distinct
        # orange backdrop. Pre-API-26 fallback (the legacy
        # `mipmap-*/ic_launcher.webp`) is left as-is; the homescreen
        # launcher will use the round / squircle adaptive icon on every
        # device this side of 2018.
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml" <<'COLORS_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<resources>
    <color name="ic_launcher_background">#D97706</color>
</resources>
COLORS_EOF
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml" <<'ICON_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<adaptive-icon xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
  <background android:drawable="@color/ic_launcher_background"/>
  <foreground android:drawable="@mipmap/ic_launcher_adaptive_fore"/>
</adaptive-icon>
ICON_EOF

        # applicationId suffix. dx writes `applicationId = "org.freenet.river"`
        # into build.gradle.kts on every regen. We rewrite to add a
        # `.debug` suffix so the debug APK installs side-by-side with
        # the release. The Kotlin namespace stays
        # `org.freenet.river` — that's the BuildConfig package, not the
        # install id. Idempotent: if the file already has `.debug`, the
        # regex doesn't match and the file is unchanged.
        perl -i -pe 's/applicationId\s*=\s*"org\.freenet\.river"$/applicationId = "org.freenet.river.debug"/' \
            "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/build.gradle.kts"

        echo "  ✓ Applied debug variant transforms (label, icon color, applicationId .debug)"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "ERROR: unknown RIVER_VARIANT=$RIVER_VARIANT (expected 'release' or 'debug')" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

echo "Overlay applied successfully."

2	 * River MainActivity — extends the dx-generated WryActivity to start
3	 * RiverNodeService as a foreground service immediately on launch.
4	 *
5	 * Without this, Android's OOM killer can — and on Pixel-class devices
6	 * typically does — reap the process within seconds of the user
7	 * backgrounding the app, dropping every peer connection the embedded
8	 * Freenet node has built up. With the service running, the process is
9	 * categorised FOREGROUND_SERVICE for as long as the user keeps River
10	 * installed and the user hasn't tapped the "Stop" action.
11	 *
12	 * This file is part of the `ui/android/` overlay copied into
13	 * `target/dx/river-ui/.../kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/` by
14	 * `scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh`. It overwrites the empty
15	 * MainActivity stub dx generates. If dx regenerates the stub on a
16	 * fresh build, the overlay script re-applies on top.
17	 */
18	package dev.dioxus.main
19	
20	import android.Manifest
21	import android.content.pm.PackageManager
22	import android.os.Build
23	import android.os.Bundle
24	import android.webkit.WebView
25	import androidx.core.app.ActivityCompat
26	import androidx.webkit.WebSettingsCompat
27	import androidx.webkit.WebViewFeature
28	
29	// re-export buildconfig down from the parent (matches the dx stub)
30	import org.freenet.river.BuildConfig
31	typealias BuildConfig = BuildConfig
32	
33	class MainActivity : WryActivity() {
34	    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
35	        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
36	
37	        // POST_NOTIFICATIONS is a runtime permission on API 33+ — without
38	        // it the foreground-service notification is hidden, defeating
39	        // the "ongoing presence" UX. We ask once on first launch; if
40	        // denied, the FGS still runs but is invisible to the user (which
41	        // is fine — Android keeps the process alive either way).
42	        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.TIRAMISU) {
43	            val granted = ActivityCompat.checkSelfPermission(
44	                this,
45	                Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS,
46	            ) == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
47	            if (!granted) {
48	                ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(
49	                    this,
50	                    arrayOf(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS),
51	                    REQUEST_CODE_POST_NOTIFICATIONS,
52	                )
53	            }
54	        }
55	
56	        RiverNodeService.start(this)
57	    }
58	
59	    // Permit the WebView to report the system `prefers-color-scheme` to
60	    // the page. WITHOUT this, the WebView always reports `light`
61	    // regardless of the device's Dark theme setting, so our CSS
62	    // `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block in tailwind.css never
63	    // fires on Android. Pair with the `<meta name="color-scheme"
64	    // content="light dark">` Dioxus emits in App() — that meta tells the
65	    // WebView "this page handles both schemes," which suppresses
66	    // WebView's own algorithmic darkening so our CSS drives entirely.
67	    // Without the meta, enabling this would double-invert the page.
68	    override fun onWebViewCreate(webView: WebView) {
69	        super.onWebViewCreate(webView)
70	        // Permit the WebView to surface the system color scheme to the
71	        // page when our CSS declares it handles dark mode. Required pair
72	        // with `parent="@style/Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar"` in
73	        // `res/values/styles.xml` — without the DayNight theme, the
74	        // activity is locked light and the WebView's
75	        // `prefers-color-scheme` query never reports dark regardless of
76	        // this setting.
77	        if (WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported(WebViewFeature.ALGORITHMIC_DARKENING)) {
78	            WebSettingsCompat.setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(webView.settings, true)
79	        }
80	    }
81	
82	    companion object {
83	        private const val REQUEST_CODE_POST_NOTIFICATIONS = 1001
84	    }
85	}

[package]
name = "river-ui"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
authors = ["Ian Clarke <ian@freenet.org>"]

[features]
# `web` is the default renderer (WASM in the browser, served as a Freenet
# contract). `mobile` swaps in the wry/tao webview renderer for Android/iOS.
# `dx` activates the feature matching the build platform: `web` for the web
# platform, `mobile` for `--platform android` / `--platform ios`.
default = ["web"]
web = ["dioxus/web"]
mobile = ["dioxus/mobile"]
delegate = [] # Define the delegate feature
example-data = []
no-sync = []

[dependencies]
bs58 = "0.5.0"
serde.workspace = true
# Cryptography
curve25519-dalek.workspace = true
x25519-dalek.workspace = true
# We can use rand_core in the UI crate because the wasm runs in a browser
ed25519-dalek = { workspace = true, features = ["rand_core"] }
sha2.workspace = true
aes-gcm.workspace = true

# Randomness
rand.workspace = true
getrandom = { version = "0.2.15", features = ["js", "wasm-bindgen", "js-sys"], default-features = false }

# UI Framework — renderer selected via the crate's `web`/`mobile` features
# (see [features] above) so the same source builds for web and Android.
dioxus = { version = "0.7.3" }
dioxus-free-icons = { version = "0.10.0", features = ["font-awesome-brands", "font-awesome-regular", "font-awesome-solid"] }

# Web-related
web-sys = { workspace = true, features = [
    "Clipboard",
    "Document",
    "DomTokenList",
    "Element",
    "EventTarget",
    "CssStyleDeclaration",
    "HtmlAnchorElement",
    "HtmlElement",
    "HtmlTextAreaElement",
    "MouseEvent",
    "IntersectionObserver",
    "IntersectionObserverEntry",
    "IntersectionObserverInit",
    "Navigator",
    "Notification",
    "NotificationOptions",
    "NotificationPermission",
    "Storage",
    "VisibilityState",
    "Window",
    "Crypto",
    "Headers",
    "Response",
    "UrlSearchParams"
] }
wasm-bindgen.workspace = true
wasm-bindgen-futures.workspace = true
lipsum = "0.9.1"

# Utilities
blake3.workspace = true
chrono.workspace = true
markdown = "1.0.0-alpha.21"
ciborium = "0.2.2"
js-sys = "0.3.64"
thiserror = "2.0.12"
log = "0.4" # Add log crate
# Compile-time gate so `debug!`/`trace!` macros are dropped entirely in
# release builds. This is belt-and-suspenders on top of the runtime
# filter `dioxus_logger` sets up (Info in release, Debug in dev) — if
# that runtime filter ever regresses, the macros still won't emit. See
# https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/level_filters/index.html#compile-time-filters
tracing = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "release_max_level_info"] }

# Internal dependencies
river-core = { workspace = true, features = ["ecies", "ecies-randomized", "migration"] }

# Freenet dependencies
freenet-scaffold.workspace = true
freenet-stdlib = { workspace = true, features = ["net"] }

futures = "0.3.30"
futures-timer = "3.0.3"

# Native (non-wasm) deps: tokio drives the synchronizer's spawn_local
# shim and the embedded freenet node. `tokio-tungstenite` is the native
# WebSocket transport that freenet-stdlib's `regular` WebApi uses; River
# also constructs it directly in the native ConnectionManager. Adding
# both here keeps the dep visible to `cargo check` on the host (which is
# what CI's `cargo test -p river-ui --bins` runs against), not only the
# Android build.
[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "sync"] }
tokio-tungstenite = { version = "0.27", features = ["rustls-tls-native-roots"] }

# Embedded Freenet node, Android-only. Pulls wasmtime + redb + the
# WebSocket client API server in-process so the UI's synchronizer can
# connect to a node running on the device. `freenet 0.2.64` pairs with
# `freenet-stdlib 0.8` (River's workspace pin — unchanged from 0.2.61
# because freenet 0.2.62/3/4 stayed on stdlib 0.8). See the vendored
# copy at `vendor/freenet/` and the workspace `[patch.crates-io]` entry.
# Version MUST track the live network's deployed gateway version or new
# peers are rejected at handshake with `Version mismatch` (see the
# diagnostics page at `http://127.0.0.1:7509/`).
[target.'cfg(target_os = "android")'.dependencies]
freenet = { version = "0.2.64", default-features = false, features = ["redb", "websocket", "wasmtime-backend", "trace"] }
# `node_runtime::run_node` returns `anyhow::Result` and uses the
# `anyhow!` macro for error wrapping around the freenet startup
# sequence — it's freenet's own error idiom so we follow it.
anyhow = "1"
# JNI bridge used to resolve the app's private files dir at runtime via
# `Context.getFilesDir()`. `ndk-context` provides the
# `JavaVM` + `Activity` handles that ndk-glue / wry / tao publish on
# Android startup; we use them as the JNI entry point rather than
# trying to reach into Dioxus's internal renderer state.
jni = "0.21"
ndk-context = "0.1"

# Add this section for the build script
[build-dependencies]
chrono = "0.4"
toml = "0.8"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(android): persist imported room + deterministic example-data keys

Three related fixes for the "Import ID" flow on Android example-data
builds:

1. example_data.rs uses per-room deterministic seed bytes for self /
   owner / other-member SigningKeys instead of OsRng. Same owner_vk on
   every launch → HashMap merge in the chat-delegate load path dedups
   instead of accumulating 3·N entries after N launches (the bug Ivvor
   reported in freenet/river#26).

2. chat_delegate.rs drops the cfg(not(feature = "example-data")) gates
   around fire_load_rooms_request() / do_save_rooms_to_delegate(). The
   gates were overcorrection for #26 — they also blocked REAL rooms
   (e.g. via "Import ID") from persisting in example-data builds. With
   the deterministic-key fix above, load+save can run unconditionally
   because the example rooms now collapse on merge rather than
   multiplying.

3. members.rs (ImportIdentityModal): on successful import, kick off a
   save_rooms_to_delegate() in a safe_spawn_local so the imported
   room is written to delegate storage IMMEDIATELY. Without this, the
   rooms_data blob doesn't update until the room_synchronizer merges
   network state — if the user closes the app before then, or the
   network is unreachable, the imported room evaporates on next launch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -10

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(android): native notifications for new messages

Wire the in-room new-message notifier (existing on the web build via
the browser Notification API) through to a real Android notification.

Surface area:

- RiverNodeService.kt grows a second notification channel
  ("river_messages", IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT so the alert is heads-up while
  the user is in another app or on the lock screen — distinct from the
  IMPORTANCE_LOW channel the foreground-service ongoing notification
  uses). A new @JvmStatic postMessageNotification(context, title, body,
  tag) builds the NotificationCompat instance, sets the tap PendingIntent
  to relaunch MainActivity, and calls NotificationManagerCompat.notify
  keyed on `tag` (stable per room) + a constant id, so subsequent
  messages in the same room replace the previous notification instead
  of stacking. POST_NOTIFICATIONS SecurityException is caught — if the
  user declined the runtime permission on first launch the call is a
  no-op (logged) rather than crashing the worker thread.

- node_runtime.rs grows a `post_message_notification(title, body, tag)`
  JNI helper that resolves the JavaVM + Activity via ndk_context,
  attaches the current thread, and calls into the Kotlin static. Every
  failure mode (VM lookup, thread attach, NewString, NoSuchMethodError)
  is logged at warn! and returns — JNI hiccups never abort the
  freenet-worker runtime.

- notifications.rs::show_notification, previously a non-wasm32 no-op,
  routes through that helper on Android. Body is "{sender}: {preview}"
  (or just the preview for grouped "N new messages" alerts). Tag uses
  MemberId::from(room_key) so it's stable per room across the lifetime
  of the install.

Foreground tracking:

- MainActivity.onStart / onStop call into a second JNI export,
  Java_dev_dioxus_main_MainActivity_nativeSetForeground, which flips a
  pub static AtomicBool in node_runtime.rs.
- notifications::is_document_visible() on Android now reads that flag.
  Without this, the existing "skip notification if room is current AND
  visible" guard would also suppress alerts the moment the user
  backgrounded the app — defeating the whole feature. With it, the
  guard mirrors the web build's document.visibility_state semantics:
  current room + foreground = no alert; current room + backgrounded
  = alert; other room either way = alert.

Verified on a Pixel 10 Pro XL:
- Both the release "River" and dev "River Debug" APKs install side by
  side, boot the embedded node, and establish peer connections within
  seconds (logcat: NAT traversal connection established / Synthetic
  auth_token registered).
- Home button → "Activity foreground state: false"; relaunch →
  "Activity foreground state: true". Round-trips cleanly across
  multiple cycles.
- The JNI bridge for postMessageNotification compiles cleanly for
  aarch64-linux-android and uses the same ndk_context handle pattern
  as the existing nativeOnServiceStop path. Live end-to-end test
  pending receipt of a real inbound message; on a JNI signature
  mismatch the warn! in post_message_notification would surface in
  logcat without crashing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -10

1	//! Embedded Freenet node (Android-only at runtime, portable at the
2	//! type level so host `cargo test` can exercise the no-JNI fallback
3	//! paths).
4	//!
5	//! On Android, `start_embedded_node` spawns a dedicated tokio
6	//! multi-thread runtime on a background OS thread and drives the
7	//! freenet node's network-mode event loop on it. The node binds its
8	//! WebSocket client API at the default `127.0.0.1:7509`; River's
9	//! `ConnectionManager` (native impl in
10	//! `freenet_api/connection_manager.rs`) connects to that endpoint.
11	//!
12	//! The node is *separate* from the Dioxus runtime — it owns its own
13	//! tokio reactor so the UI's event loop isn't sharing scheduling
14	//! pressure with wasmtime contract execution, and so that long-lived
15	//! node tasks (peer connection recv loops, transport drivers) don't
16	//! have to be `'static` against the Dioxus scope.
17	//!
18	//! **Network mode, not Local.** A Local-mode node only serves what's
19	//! been PUT to its own stores — Android users could create their own
20	//! rooms but could not join any room shared via invitation link,
21	//! because the network state never reaches their device. Network
22	//! mode makes the device a real Freenet peer that fetches contracts
23	//! and states through peers and gateways. See
24	//! `openspec/changes/android-bundled-node/design.md` decision #2 for
25	//! the full rationale and the mobile-NAT risks.
26	//!
27	//! Remaining caveats (tracked in the OpenSpec change's tasks.md):
28	//! - No foreground service yet — Android may kill the process when
29	//!   the app backgrounds (tasks 5.x).
30	//!
31	//! On non-Android targets, `start_embedded_node` is a no-op stub so
32	//! the module compiles for host `cargo check` / `cargo test` without
33	//! pulling in freenet, tokio, jni, or ndk-context.
34	
35	use std::path::PathBuf;
36	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
37	use std::sync::OnceLock;
38	
39	/// Tracks whether the Android activity is currently visible to the user.
40	///
41	/// Toggled by `MainActivity.onStart` / `onStop` via the
42	/// `Java_dev_dioxus_main_MainActivity_nativeSetForeground` JNI export
43	/// below. Read by `notifications::is_document_visible` on Android so
44	/// the new-message notifier matches the web build's semantics: a room
45	/// the user is "currently viewing" only suppresses notifications while
46	/// the app is on-screen. Once the user backgrounds the app (Home, app
47	/// switcher, screen off) every room — including the one they had open
48	/// — should fire a notification.
49	///
50	/// Default `true` so any code path that runs before the first
51	/// lifecycle callback (cold start of the embedded node thread, async
52	/// setup work) treats the app as visible. The lifecycle tick reaches
53	/// `onStart` within milliseconds of activity creation, so the
54	/// transient window is benign.
55	pub static ANDROID_FOREGROUND: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(true);
56	
57	/// Read the foreground flag. Always returns `true` off-Android since
58	/// host targets have no equivalent visibility model.
59	pub fn android_is_foreground() -> bool {
60	    #[cfg(target_os = "android")]
61	    {
62	        ANDROID_FOREGROUND.load(Ordering::Acquire)
63	    }
64	    #[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]
65	    {
66	        true
67	    }
68	}
69	
70	/// Synthetic auth token registered with the embedded node's
71	/// `OriginContractMap` at startup, surfaced here so the UI's loopback
72	/// WebSocket dial can attach it as `?authToken=…`.
73	///
74	/// **Why this exists.** The chat-delegate's `check_origin` rejects any
75	/// `DelegateRequest::ApplicationMessage` whose `MessageOrigin` is
76	/// `None` with `"missing message origin"`. On the web build the gateway
77	/// shell injects `window.__FREENET_AUTH_TOKEN__`, and the WS handler
78	/// looks the token up in a map populated when the shell HTML was served
79	/// to mint the page's contract origin. On Android the UI loads via wry's
80	/// custom protocol, never goes through a gateway shell, and would
81	/// otherwise dial the loopback WS anonymously — every delegate save
82	/// times out and the room is lost on restart.
83	///
84	/// We close that gap by pre-registering a random token under River's
85	/// **published web-container contract id** (so the attested origin
86	/// matches what web clients send) in `serve_client_api_with_listener_and_contracts`'s
87	/// returned map, then publishing the token here for
88	/// `connection_manager` to pick up. `OnceLock` because the node starts
89	/// exactly once per process and the token is immutable thereafter.
90	pub static EMBEDDED_AUTH_TOKEN: OnceLock<String> = OnceLock::new();
91	
92	/// Hardcoded fallback for the embedded Freenet node's storage dir.
93	///
94	/// Matches the package id in `ui/Dioxus.toml` (`org.freenet.river`).
95	/// On a real device the runtime path comes from
96	/// `Context.getFilesDir()` via JNI ([`android_files_dir`]) — this
97	/// constant is only used when the JNI lookup fails (emulator without
98	/// an attached Activity, unusual launch path, etc.) so the node can
99	/// still boot rather than aborting.
100	pub(crate) const FREENET_DATA_DIR_FALLBACK: &str = "/data/data/org.freenet.river/files/freenet";
101	
102	/// Resolve the app's private files dir at runtime via JNI.
103	///
104	/// Walks the standard Android startup handles:
105	/// 1. `ndk_context::android_context()` exposes the `JavaVM` + the
106	///    activity's `Context` jobject, published by ndk-glue / wry / tao
107	///    during native startup.
108	/// 2. Attach the current thread to the VM.
109	/// 3. Call `Context.getFilesDir() -> java/io/File`.
110	/// 4. Call `File.getAbsolutePath() -> java/lang/String`.
111	/// 5. Decode the Java string to a Rust `String` and join `"freenet"`
112	///    onto it, giving the node its own subdirectory under the app's
113	///    private files area.
114	///
115	/// Returns `None` on any JNI failure (ndk-context not populated, VM
116	/// attach failure, `NoSuchMethodError`) AND on every non-Android
117	/// target. Callers fall back to [`FREENET_DATA_DIR_FALLBACK`] and
118	/// emit a `warn!` so the failure is visible in logcat.
119	#[cfg(target_os = "android")]
120	pub(crate) fn android_files_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
121	    use jni::objects::{JObject, JString};
122	    use jni::JavaVM;
123	
124	    let ctx = ndk_context::android_context();
125	    let vm = unsafe { JavaVM::from_raw(ctx.vm().cast()) }.ok()?;
126	    let activity = unsafe { JObject::from_raw(ctx.context().cast()) };
127	
128	    let mut env = vm.attach_current_thread().ok()?;
129	
130	    // Context.getFilesDir() -> java/io/File
131	    let files_dir = env
132	        .call_method(&activity, "getFilesDir", "()Ljava/io/File;", &[])
133	        .ok()?
134	        .l()
135	        .ok()?;
136	
137	    // File.getAbsolutePath() -> java/lang/String
138	    let path_jstr = env
139	        .call_method(&files_dir, "getAbsolutePath", "()Ljava/lang/String;", &[])
140	        .ok()?
141	        .l()
142	        .ok()?;
143	
144	    let path_jstr: JString = path_jstr.into();
145	    let rust_path: String = env.get_string(&path_jstr).ok()?.into();
146	
147	    Some(PathBuf::from(rust_path).join("freenet"))
148	}
149	
150	/// Host stub: no Activity, no JNI, always return `None` so the
151	/// caller falls back to [`FREENET_DATA_DIR_FALLBACK`].
152	#[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]
153	pub(crate) fn android_files_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
154	    None
155	}
156	
157	/// Compute the node's storage dir, with the JNI lookup tried first
158	/// and a fall-back to the hardcoded package-private path on failure.
159	pub(crate) fn resolve_data_dir() -> PathBuf {
160	    android_files_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(FREENET_DATA_DIR_FALLBACK))
161	}
162	
163	#[cfg(target_os = "android")]
164	mod android {
165	    use super::*;
166	    use std::path::Path;
167	    use std::sync::Mutex;
168

170	    // `freenet::client_events` is `pub(crate)`; the public re-exports

input.command:
gh pr create \
  --repo freenet/river \
  --base main \
  --head SalvatoreT:android-bundled-node \
  --title "feat(android): bundled Freenet node — production Android variant" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes the [android-bundled-node](openspec/changes/android-bundled-node/) OpenSpec change: River on Android now runs as a real Freenet peer with an in-process node, persistent storage, peer-survivable foreground service, side-by-side release + debug variants, and native heads-up notifications for new messages.

## Summary

- **Embedded Freenet node** (`ui/src/node_runtime.rs`) — spawns a dedicated tokio runtime on a background OS thread, binds the WS client API at `127.0.0.1:7509`, and runs in Network mode against the published gateways (nova / vega + auto-discovered peers).
- **JNI storage path resolution** — `Context.getFilesDir()` via JNI gives the node its own subdirectory under the app's private files area; a hardcoded `org.freenet.river` fallback keeps the node bootable if the JNI lookup ever fails.
- **Foreground service** (`RiverNodeService.kt`) — keeps the embedded node alive when the user backgrounds the app. Ongoing low-importance notification + Stop action; `onDestroy` JNI-signals a parked `oneshot::Sender` so the node drops cleanly instead of being SIGKILL'd.
- **Synthetic auth_token** — pre-registered with the embedded node's `OriginContractMap` under River's published web-container contract id, so the chat delegate's `check_origin` accepts every `ApplicationMessage` instead of timing them all out.
- **Bundled fallback gateways** — `gateways.toml` + nova/vega X25519 PEMs staged into the node's config dir on offline first launch so the node can still bootstrap without freenet.org reachability.
- **stdlib 0.8 WASM rebuild** — chat-delegate `343272eb…` + room_contract `dba68bdd…` rebuilt against `freenet-stdlib 0.8`, with V24/V25 legacy entries recorded in `legacy_delegates.toml` / `common/legacy_room_contracts.toml`.
- **River + River Debug variants** — release APK installs as `org.freenet.river` ("River"); the debug variant carries example-data, `applicationId .debug` suffix, and a distinct adaptive-icon background so the two installs are visually distinguishable.
- **Native new-message notifications** — Rust → JNI bridge to `RiverNodeService.postMessageNotification` posts a heads-up alert on a separate `river_messages` channel. Tag-keyed per room so subsequent messages replace rather than stack. Foreground/background tracker via `MainActivity.onStart`/`onStop` lets `is_document_visible()` return the right thing on Android so backgrounded users get notified even for the room they had open.
- **A grab-bag of mobile UX polish** committed along the way: paste-invitation modal (Android has no `?invitation=` URL handler), dx default → River dolphin icon, DayNight theme respect, system clipboard via JNI, fully-routed `safe_spawn_local` to avoid the `wasm_bindgen_futures::CREATE_TASK` extern panic on aarch64.

## What this PR does NOT close

Three OpenSpec tasks (7.2 / 7.3 / 7.4) plus their two downstream acceptance scenarios (8.2 / 8.3) remain blocked on Ian Clarke. Republishing the River web container at stdlib 0.8 requires the canonical signing key in `~/.config/river/web-container-keys.toml`, which only lives on his host — signing with any other key would change the contract id and strand every existing user's room data. Path forward is documented in `openspec/changes/android-bundled-node/tasks.md` § 7.2.

Until that web republish lands, Android users live in a different contract namespace from existing web users (so cross-platform invitation flows can't be verified end-to-end yet).

## Verification

- **Real-device peer connectivity** on Pixel 10 Pro XL (mustang, Android 14+):
  - `NAT traversal connection established` against nova / vega / a third gateway-routed peer within ~10 s of cold launch
  - 5-peer ring reporting RTT-adaptive cc metrics (44–56 ms) within 30 s
  - evidence: `/tmp/claude/pixel_crash_slim.log`
- **Foreground survives background** — PID 20916 stable across Home press + 60 s sleep; `dumpsys activity services org.freenet.river` reports `isForeground=true types=0x00000001 channel=river_node_channel flags=ONGOING_EVENT|NO_CLEAR|FOREGROUND_SERVICE`; `oom_score_adj=200` (FGS-protected). UI reconnects on resume without a cold restart.
- **stdlib-0.8 migration validates** — `cargo test -p river-core --test migration_test` + `cargo test -p river-core --test room_contract_migration_test` both pass (4 tests each).
- **Native notifications smoke-tested today** — both APKs install + boot; `Activity foreground state` toggles `true` → `false` → `true` cleanly across Home + relaunch. Full inbound-message verification pending receipt of a real DM (JNI signature mismatch would log at `warn!` without crashing).
- **WASM hash check** — `cargo make check-android-wasm-hashes` clean; `cargo make sync-wasm`-produced hashes match the committed `ui/public/contracts/` + `cli/contracts/` WASMs.

## Test plan

- [ ] Cold-launch the release APK; confirm `NAT traversal connection established` within 30 s of boot.
- [ ] Background via Home; confirm FGS notification persists and the foreground state flips `false` in logcat.
- [ ] Foreground; confirm the UI reconnects without a cold restart.
- [ ] Tap the Stop action on the FGS notification; confirm `Embedded node shutdown requested by RiverNodeService.onDestroy` in logcat.
- [ ] Send a message from a parallel web client to a room the Android client is in (after the web republish lands); confirm:
  - room is in the current view + app foregrounded → no notification, message appears inline
  - room is in the current view + app backgrounded → heads-up notification fires
  - room is NOT in the current view, either state → heads-up notification fires
  - tapping the notification reopens MainActivity and lands on the right room
- [ ] Side-load on an Android 13 (API 33) device; confirm POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt fires on first launch.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1
